stories.hook: ¿Puede la estimulación cerebral en casa aliviar la depresión?
stories.headline: tDCS domiciliario reduce significativamente los síntomas depresivos en ensayo aleatorio
stories.finding: En un ensayo controlado aleatorizado de 10 semanas, 174 pacientes con trastorno depresivo mayor fueron asignados a tDCS activo en casa o a sham. El grupo activo mostró una mejora de 9,41 ± 6,25 puntos en la escala Hamilton, evidenciando una reducción clínica significativa respecto al control.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la tDCS domiciliaria es una opción viable y escalable para tratar la depresión moderada a severa, ampliando el acceso a terapias neuromoduladoras sin necesidad de visitas presenciales.
stories.paperTitle: Home-based transcranial direct current stimulation treatment for major depressive disorder: a fully remote phase 2 randomized sham-controlled trial
stories.originalAbstract: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) has been proposed as a new treatment in major depressive disorder (MDD). This is a fully remote, multisite, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized superiority trial of 10-week home-based tDCS in MDD. Participants were 18 years or older, with MDD in current depressive episode of at least moderate severity as measured using the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (mean = 19.07 ± 2.73). A total of 174 participants (120 women, 54 men) were randomized to active (n = 87, mean age = 37.09 ± 11.14 years) or sham (n = 87, mean age = 38.32 ± 10.92 years) treatment. tDCS consisted of five sessions per week for 3 weeks then three sessions per week for 7 weeks in a 10-week trial, followed by a 10-week open-label phase. Each session lasted 30 min; the anode was placed over the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and the cathode over the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (active tDCS 2 mA and sham tDCS 0 mA, with brief ramp up and down to mimic active stimulation). As the primary outcome, depressive symptoms showed significant improvement when measured using the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale: active 9.41 ± 6.25 point improvement (10-week mean = 9.58 ± 6.02) and sham 7.14 ± 6.10 point improvement (10-week mean = 11.66 ± 5.96) (95% confidence interval = 0.51-4.01, P = 0.012). There were no differences in discontinuation rates. In summary, a 10-week home-based tDCS treatment with remote supervision in MDD showed high efficacy, acceptability and safety. ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05202119.

stories.headline: Journaling de autocompasión reduce el malestar emocional en la rumiación
stories.finding: En un estudio con quince participantes que realizaron una tarea de journaling en línea bajo tres condiciones (reflexión centrada en afecto negativo, reflexión autocompasiva de afecto positivo y reappraisal cognitivo), la condición de autocompasión disminuyó significativamente la angustia subjetiva (SUDS) respecto a la condición negativa. Los análisis de efectos mixtos confirmaron que el tipo de journaling influyó de manera significativa en el nivel de malestar emocional.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo indica que integrar reflexiones autocompasivas en intervenciones breves puede atenuar el impacto emocional de la rumiación, ofreciendo a los profesionales una estrategia práctica y de bajo costo para trastornos vinculados al pensamiento repetitivo.
stories.paperTitle: Shifting the Emotional Impact of Repetitive Negative Thinking: Effects of Self- Compassion and Reappraisal Journaling
stories.journal: Digital Access to Scholarship at Harvard (DASH) (Harvard University)
stories.originalAbstract: Repetitive Negative Thinking (RNT) is commonly associated with maladaptive psychological outcomes characterized by intrusive, perseverative thought patterns. Across literature, self-compassion has repeatedly been identified as a protective factor, and theoretical models of repetitive thought (RT) suggest that its outcomes depend on the mode of engagement rather than the mere presence of RT themselves. The present study investigated whether a self-compassionate reflection influences the emotional responses to RNT within a process-focused framework amid continued RT. Fifteen participants completed a brief within-subjects online journaling task involving three conditions: negative affect–focused reflection (NA-SC), positive affect self-compassion reflection (PA-SC), and cognitive reappraisal. Emotional distress (Subjective Units of Distress Scale; SUDS) and perceived thought negativity were assessed following each condition, and state RNT (RTQ-10) and state self-compassion (SCS-SF) measures were assessed at baseline, and following the NA-SC and PA-SC conditions. Mixed-effects models for repeated measures indicated a significant effect of journaling condition on emotional distress, F(2, 28) = 22.25, p .0001, with distress highest following NA-SC (M = 48.0), lower following PA-SC (M = 33.3), and lowest following reappraisal (M = 26.0). Perceived thought negativity also differed across conditions, F(2, 28) = 7.72, p = .0021, whereas state RNT levels did not significantly change (p = .1986). State self-compassion increased during PA-SC relative to NA-SC, F(1, 14) = 6.71, p = .021. Findings suggest that modifying how individuals engage with RT may lead to reductions of emotional consequences without reducing thought frequency, supporting process-oriented models of RT.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo se sincronizan cerebro y corazón ante una amenaza?
stories.headline: Acoplamiento cerebro‑cardíaco aumenta durante amenazas inmediatas en trastornos de ansiedad
stories.finding: En un estudio con 90 participantes (trastorno de pánico, trastorno de ansiedad social y controles) se utilizó un paradigma de condicionamiento de amenaza con estímulos faciales y ruido aversivo. El ruido generó fuerte aceleración cardíaca y un ERP N100, evidenciando acoplamiento significativo entre respuestas corticales y cardíacas intraindividualmente.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo revela que la sincronía cerebro‑cardíaca es un marcador fisiológico de la respuesta a amenazas en la ansiedad, lo que podría guiar intervenciones biofeedback o tratamientos dirigidos a regular la activación autonómica.
stories.paperTitle: Brain-heart coupling in response to imminent threat in panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, and healthy controls
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: Imminent threat does not only capture attention but also triggers defensive psychophysiological responses associated with fight-flight-freeze behavior. However, within-subject associations between central markers of attentional stimulus processing and peripheral components of early defensive activation (e.g., cardiac acceleration) are not well understood. These associations may be especially important in understanding dynamics of anxiety disorders that are characterized by cardiovascular symptoms such as panic disorder. METHODS: We analyzed data from N = 90 participants with panic disorder (PD), social anxiety disorder (SAD), as well as healthy controls (CG) who completed a threat conditioning paradigm with face stimuli as conditioned stimuli (CS) and an aversive white noise burst as unconditioned stimulus (US). In addition to univariate analyses of ERPs and heartbeat, single-trial EEG evoked by the noise burst at centromedial sites and heart period were used to calculate intraindividual coupling of unconditioned cortico-cardiac responses. RESULTS: The noise burst evoked strong cardiac acceleration and an event-related potential with a pronounced N100 component. Importantly, the magnitude of single-trial cardiac acceleration was predicted within individuals by the preceding single-trial N100 magnitude. This cortico-cardiac coupling, but not the N100 component or cardiac acceleration per se, was enhanced in individuals with panic disorder compared to social anxiety disorder, with intermediate levels of coupling observed in healthy controls. CONCLUSION: The present results suggest a central role of early attentional stimulus processing in subsequent cardiac defensive responses. Furthermore, they indicate that cortico-cardiac defensive responses may be altered in individuals with panic disorder specifically, rather than in anxiety disorders in general.

stories.hook: ¿Qué terapia alivia mejor el PTSD infantil?
stories.headline: CBT y terapias focalizadas demuestran eficacia contra PTSD en jóvenes
stories.finding: La revisión sistemática encontró que la terapia cognitivo-conductual (CBT) y la terapia cognitivo-conductual focalizada en trauma (TF‑CBT) son tratamientos efectivos para el trastorno de estrés post‑raumático en niños y adolescentes. También se observaron beneficios de EMDR, terapia sistémica, terapia de juego y exposición, aunque la evidencia varía según la edad y la gravedad.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo orienta a los clínicos a priorizar intervenciones basadas en CBT para jóvenes con PTSD, optimizando recursos y mejorando pronósticos de desarrollo.
stories.paperTitle: Clinical Efficacy of Psychotherapeutic Interventions for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Analysis
stories.originalAbstract: Background: This systematic review aggregates research on psychotherapeutic interventions for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) in children and adolescents. PTSD in this demographic presents differently from adults, necessitating tailored therapeutic approaches. In children and adolescents, PTSD arises from exposure to severe danger, interpersonal violence, or abuse, leading to significant behavioral and emotional disturbances that jeopardize long-term development. The review focuses on describing PTSD within two age groups, children (6 to 12 years) and adolescents (12 to 18 years), while evaluating the effectiveness of various clinical interventions aimed at this condition. Methods: Utilizing the PRISMA guidelines, this review systematically examines studies that assess clinical interventions for PTSD in the younger population. Results: Key symptoms of PTSD in children and adolescents include avoidance, overstimulation, flashbacks, depression, and anxiety. The review identifies several effective treatments, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Trauma-Focused CBT (TF-CBT), Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR), Systemic Therapy, Play Therapy, Exposure Therapy, Relaxation Techniques, and Psychodynamic Psychotherapy. Particularly, TF-CBT is highlighted as the most effective and commonly used method in treating childhood and adolescent PTSD, as supported by most of the studies reviewed. Conclusions: A significant outcome of this study is the short-term effectiveness of CBT in reducing PTSD symptoms in children and adolescents. The findings underline the importance of psychotherapeutic interventions and mark a substantial advancement in understanding PTSD in young populations. It is crucial for practitioners to integrate various psychotherapeutic strategies into their practice to improve patient outcomes and treatment efficacy.

stories.hook: ¿Pueden las experiencias positivas contrarrestar el trauma infantil?
stories.headline: Experiencias infantiles positivas moderan el efecto de los ACEs sobre la salud mental adolescente
stories.finding: En una muestra de 700 adolescentes, los ACEs se relacionaron significativamente con peor salud mental. La rumiación y la resiliencia psicológica medieron indirectamente esa relación de forma secuencial, y las experiencias infantiles positivas moderaron tanto la asociación ACEs‑salud mental como los caminos mediadores.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que fortalecer experiencias positivas en la infancia y promover resiliencia puede atenuar el impacto de los traumas tempranos, ofreciendo una vía preventiva y terapéutica para mejorar la salud mental de los adolescentes.
stories.paperTitle: Adverse and positive childhood experiences in relation to adolescent mental health: sequential indirect associations
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Accumulating evidence has linked adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) to adolescent mental health problems, whereas positive childhood experiences (PCEs) may serve a protective function. Guided by the stress-vulnerability model, this study examined the associations between ACEs and adolescent mental health, and further investigated the indirect pathways via rumination and psychological resilience, as well as the moderating role of PCEs. Methods: A total of 700 adolescents were recruited and completed validated measures of ACEs, PCEs, rumination, psychological resilience, and mental health. Indirect association and moderation models were tested using the PROCESS macro in SPSS, and the significance of indirect associations was evaluated with bootstrap confidence intervals. Results: ACEs were significantly associated with poorer mental health. Rumination and psychological resilience each showed significant indirect associations, and together formed a significant sequential indirect association in the cross-sectional model. In addition, PCEs significantly moderated the associations between ACEs and mental health, between ACEs and rumination, and between ACEs and psychological resilience. Conclusion: These findings suggest a complex pattern of associations between ACEs and adolescent mental health: rumination and psychological resilience may be involved in a sequential indirect association, and PCEs were associated with a protective moderating pattern. The results may inform risk identification for adolescent mental health and the development of family- and school-based intervention strategies.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo influyen los estilos de apego en nuestras defensas psicológicas?
stories.headline: Inseguridad del apego se asocia con defensas inmaduras, seguridad con defensas maduras
stories.finding: El análisis de veinte estudios empíricos revela que los individuos con apego inseguro emplean con mayor frecuencia defensas inmaduras, mientras que el apego seguro se relaciona con defensas maduras. Además, el apego ansioso muestra una asociación específica con proyección, escisión y devaluación.
stories.takeaway: Comprender esta relación permite a los terapeutas orientar intervenciones que fortalezcan el apego seguro y fomenten defensas maduras, mejorando la regulación emocional y la resiliencia clínica.
stories.paperTitle: The relationship between defense mechanisms and attachment: a narrative review
stories.journal: Research in Psychotherapy Psychopathology Process and Outcome
stories.originalAbstract: While a substantial number of studies investigate the nuances and clinical relevance of attachment styles and defense mechanisms separately, relatively few studies have explored the relationship between attachment styles and defense mechanisms. We aimed to provide a narrative review of empirical studies that used validated measures to assess the relationship between defense mechanisms and attachment styles in adolescents or adults. Twenty peer-reviewed studies published over the past 30 years were included. Except for one study involving high school students, all others focused on adults, mostly from community samples, with a few including clinical populations. Most studies employed various self-report questionnaires, though several used observer-rated or interview-based methods, with the majority using a cross-sectional design; a few studies used experimental and longitudinal designs as well. The studies' findings indicate an association between insecure attachment and greater use of immature defenses, while secure attachment is associated with more mature defenses. Anxious attachment was particularly linked to defenses such as projection, splitting, and devaluation, whereas avoidant attachment was associated with emotional suppression and denial. A subset of studies examined changes in these constructs during psychotherapy, suggesting that both defense mechanisms and attachment security may improve over time, and indicating the potential importance of reflective functioning as a mediator, as well as depressive immature defenses as obstacles to change. These results underscore the clinical relevance of assessing both attachment and defensive functioning and highlight the importance of addressing them as potential mechanisms of change in clinical contexts.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo medir la regulación emocional infantil con precisión?
stories.headline: Nuevo inventario valida la regulación emocional en niños de 3 a 12 años
stories.finding: Se propuso un marco conceptual y se creó el Emotional Competence Inventory for Children (ECIC). En dos muestras (N = 695) los análisis factoriales confirmaron cuatro dimensiones, incluida la regulación emocional, y el instrumento mostró propiedades psicométricas adecuadas.
stories.takeaway: Este inventario brinda a clínicos y investigadores una herramienta estandarizada para evaluar la regulación emocional y otras competencias en la infancia, facilitando detección temprana y diseño de intervenciones basadas en evidencia.
stories.paperTitle: Child emotional competence: a conceptual organizing framework and parent-report measure of emotion reasoning, emotion stability, emotion regulation, and empathy
stories.journal: Frontiers in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction Emotional competence (EC) plays a vital role in children's development, well-being, and mental health outcomes. However, the field lacks consensus on definitions and measurement approaches, leading to inconsistencies and limitations in understanding and assessing EC. Methods This paper presents a conceptual organizing framework for EC that integrates and clarifies the various components of emotional functioning. Additionally, a new measure, the Emotional Competence Inventory for Children (ECIC), was developed and validated to assess EC among children ages 3–12 years based on the proposed framework. The study involved two separate samples ( N = 695) recruited through Amazon's Mechanical Turk. Data analysis included exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, measurement invariance testing, and assessments of reliability and validity. Results Results supported the four components of EC: Emotion Reasoning, Emotion Stability, Emotion Regulation, and Empathy. Subscales of Emotion Reasoning and Emotion Stability were identified, providing nuanced insights into emotional development. The ECIC demonstrated promising psychometric properties, including evidence of measurement invariance across several demographic groups, although full scalar invariance was not established across all groups. The unique associations of ECIC scales/subscales shed light on their differential associations with child health outcomes, aiding precision-medicine approaches and intervention efforts. Discussion The validated ECIC measure offers an important tool for assessing EC and informing future personalized treatment research and assessment strategies. This conceptual organizing framework and accompanying measure contribute to advancing our understanding of EC, supporting children's emotional development, and promoting their overall well-being. Future research should further validate and refine the framework while investigating its applicability in diverse populations and treatment settings.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la privación de sueño alterar nuestros relojes genéticos?
stories.headline: La privación de sueño reduce CLOCK y BMAL1 y aumenta PER1 en humanos
stories.finding: En 81 participantes, una noche de privación de sueño redujo la expresión de CLOCK y BMAL1 e incrementó PER1. PER1 se correlacionó positivamente con el tiempo total y la duración del sueño NREM, y negativamente con la latencia y la actividad de ondas alfa, beta y delta.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que la privación de sueño modula directamente genes centrales del reloj circadiano, ofreciendo posibles biomarcadores y objetivos terapéuticos para trastornos relacionados con el sueño y la salud mental.
stories.paperTitle: Circadian Rhythm Genes and Their Association with Sleep and Sleep Restriction
stories.originalAbstract: Deprivation of sleep (DS) and its effects on circadian rhythm gene expression are not well understood despite their influence on various physiological and psychological processes. This study aimed to elucidate the changes in the expression of circadian rhythm genes following a night of sleep and DS. Their correlation with sleep architecture and physical activity was also examined. The study included 81 participants who underwent polysomnography (PSG) and DS with actigraphy. Blood samples were collected after PSG and DS. Expression levels of brain and muscle ARNT-like 1 (BMAL1), circadian locomotor output cycles kaput (CLOCK), neuronal PAS domain protein 2 (NPAS2), period 1 (PER1), cryptochrome 1 (CRY1) and nuclear receptor subfamily 1 group D member 1 (NR1D1) were analyzed using qRT-PCR. DS decreased the expression of CLOCK and BMAL1 while increasing PER1. PER1 expression correlated positively with total sleep time and non-rapid-eye-movement (NREM) sleep duration and negatively with sleep latency, alpha, beta and delta waves in the O1A2 lead. Physical activity during DS showed positive correlations with CLOCK, BMAL1, and CRY1. The findings highlight the role of PER1 in modulating sleep patterns, suggesting potential targets for managing sleep-related disorders. Further research is essential to deepen the understanding of these relationships and their implications.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la autocompasión superar al mindfulness tradicional a largo plazo?
stories.headline: El programa de Autocompasión Consciente muestra beneficios sostenidos similares al MBSR durante un año
stories.finding: En un ensayo cuasi‑randomizado con 170 participantes, tanto el programa Mindful Self‑Compassion (MSC) como el Mindfulness‑Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) mejoraron significativamente ansiedad, depresión, estrés percibido, afecto y flexibilidad psicológica respecto al control. Estas mejoras se mantuvieron durante un año, con trayectorias similares.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo indica que la autocompasión consciente es tan eficaz como el MBSR para mejorar la salud mental y sus efectos persisten a largo plazo, ofreciendo a los profesionales una alternativa basada en evidencia para programas de prevención y tratamiento.
stories.paperTitle: Long-term effectiveness of the Mindful Self-Compassion programme compared to a Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction intervention: a quasi-randomised controlled trial involving regular mindfulness practice for 1 year
stories.originalAbstract: Introduction This study compares the Mindful Self-Compassion (MSC) programme with the Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR), a well-established intervention, and a control group, and includes 1 year of continuous practice. Methods A longitudinal quasi-RCT was conducted with measurements at baseline, post-training, 6 months and 1 year. A total of 170 individuals (75.9% female) were randomly assigned to the MSC (n = 48) and MBSR (n = 65) groups, with a non-fully randomised wait-list CG (n = 57). Results Using intention-to-treat (ITT) and per-protocol (PP) analysis strategies, results consistently indicated that standard 8-week MSC and MBSR trainings produced benefits on anxiety, depression, perceived stress, and positive and negative affect, as well as on variables related to psychological flexibility, compared with CG. These gains were maintained over a year of continuous practice in both training groups. Overall, the two programmes, MSC and MBSR, showed a similar trajectory over the measurement periods. Discussion The 8-week MSC programme and the regular practice of mindfulness and self-compassion appear to be an effective intervention for promoting mental health in the general population, with benefits similar to those derived from the practice of exercises from well-known mindfulness programmes such as MBSR.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la autocompasión frenar el síndrome del impostor?
stories.headline: La autocompasión amortigua el efecto de la competitividad en el impostor
stories.finding: En una muestra de 215 estudiantes de primer año en Indonesia, la percepción de competitividad se correlacionó negativamente con el fenómeno del impostor. Además, la autocompasión mostró una correlación negativa significativa y moderó positivamente la relación entre competitividad percibida y el impostor, reduciendo su intensidad.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que fomentar la autocompasión en entornos académicos competitivos puede proteger la autoestima y prevenir el síndrome del impostor, ofreciendo una estrategia preventiva para la salud mental estudiantil.
stories.paperTitle: The Role of Self-Compassion as A Moderating Variable : Perception of Competitiveness on The Impostor Phenomenon Among First-Year College Students
stories.journal: Jurnal Kependidikan Jurnal Hasil Penelitian dan Kajian Kepustakaan di Bidang Pendidikan Pengajaran dan Pembelajaran
stories.originalAbstract: This study aims to analyze the moderating role of self-compassion on the relationship between the perception of a competitive environment and the impostor phenomenon in a sample of 215 first-year college students in Indonesia. The study employed a quantitative approach and the data were collected using an online questionnaire consisting of three measuring instruments: Perceived Competitiveness Questionnaire (PCQ), Clance Impostor Phenomenon Scale (CIPS), and Self-Compassion Scale (SCS). Correlation analysis and moderated regression analysis were performed to test the hypotheses of the study. This study shows that the perception of competitiveness was negatively correlated with the impostor phenomenon. Additionally, self-compassion has a significant negative correlation with feelings of being an impostor. This research also reveals that self-compassion positively moderates the relationship between the perception of competitiveness and the impostor phenomenon. These findings emphasize the importance of self-compassion as a protective factor in mitigating the negative impacts of competitive academic settings and reducing potential impostor phenomenon by empowering college students with resilience and greater confidence.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el agradecimiento reducir el burnout de los voluntarios?
stories.headline: El agradecimiento de ciudadanos y supervisores disminuye el burnout mediante la motivación de servicio público
stories.finding: En una muestra de 1 692 voluntarios sanitarios comunitarios tailandeses, el agradecimiento percibido de ciudadanos y supervisores incrementó la motivación de servicio público, lo que redujo significativamente el burnout laboral. El agradecimiento gubernamental no influyó directamente en la motivación, pero potenció los efectos de los demás agradecimientos.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que reconocer a los voluntarios mediante agradecimientos cercanos puede ser una estrategia práctica y de bajo costo para fortalecer su motivación y prevenir el desgaste ocupacional, orientando políticas de gestión de recursos humanos en salud comunitaria.
stories.paperTitle: The Impacts of Multiple Sources of Gratitude on Public Service Motivation and Job Burnout Among Community Health Volunteers in Thailand
stories.journal: VOLUNTAS International Journal of Voluntary and Nonprofit Organizations
stories.originalAbstract: Community health volunteers play a crucial role in advancing public health and community welfare, yet their contributions often remain invisible in policy discourse. Grounded in self-determination theory, this study examines how three sources of gratitude—citizens, supervisors, and the government—mitigate volunteers’ job burnout. Using data from 1,692 community health volunteers in Thailand, the findings reveal that citizen and supervisor gratitude enhance public service motivation (PSM), which, in turn, reduces burnout, with citizen gratitude showing the strongest influence. While government gratitude does not shape PSM directly, it amplifies the effects of both citizen and supervisor gratitude on PSM. These findings suggest that symbolic recognition from authorities, though not sufficient in isolation, can legitimize and reinforce more proximal forms of appreciation. By examining three sources of gratitude simultaneously, and their interaction, this study extends multilevel accounts of gratitude and points to a neglected but actionable lever for managing community health volunteers.

stories.headline: El Couple Flourishing Measure supera al DAS en diagnóstico clínico
stories.finding: En una muestra española de 118 adultos en relaciones afectivo‑sexuales, el Couple Flourishing Measure discriminó mejor entre pacientes de terapia de pareja (n=67) y comunidad (n=51) que la Dyadic Adjustment Scale (AUC = 0.81 vs 0.71). Un corte preliminar de 61.5 mostró sensibilidad 0.64 y especificidad 0.94.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo brinda a los profesionales una herramienta más precisa para identificar parejas que requieren intervención terapéutica, facilitando decisiones clínicas basadas en una medida que captura el florecimiento relacional más allá de la mera satisfacción.
stories.paperTitle: Criterion‐Related Validity of the Couple Flourishing Measure in a Spanish Population: Distinguishing Outpatients From Community Participants
stories.originalAbstract: Relational (or couple) well-being has begun to be conceived from an integrative perspective that transcends mere satisfaction or stability in couples and may include dimensions such as emotional connection, joint growth, and shared purpose. This study evaluated the criterion-related validity of the Couple Flourishing Measure (CFM) in comparison with the Dyadic Adjustment Scale (DAS) in a Spanish sample of people in affective-sexual relationships (n = 118; Mage = 40.3, SD = 8.77). Differences between participants receiving affective-sexual therapy services (n = 67) and community participants (n = 51) were analyzed, as well as their discriminative ability using ROC curves. The results showed that the CFM had a greater ability to discriminate between the two groups (AUC = 0.81, 95% CI [0.74, 0.89]) than the DAS (AUC = 0.71, 95% CI [0.62, 0.81]). In turn, a preliminary cutoff score for CFM was identified (61.5), with moderate sensitivity (0.64) and high specificity (0.94). These findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the criterion-related validity of the CFM for distinguishing outpatients receiving affective-sexual therapy from community participants without previous therapeutic experience and suggest that the measure may offer complementary information beyond traditional indicators of relationship adjustment. Implications, limitations, and directions for future research are discussed.

stories.headline: La educación emprendedora en la escuela primaria fomenta el sociopreneurship en economías emergentes
stories.finding: Los datos revelan que la educación emprendedora recibida en la escuela básica se asocia positivamente con la sociopreneurship, indicando que los aprendizajes tempranos generan impresiones duraderas. En contraste, la educación emprendedora posterior muestra una asociación nula o débil, salvo en contextos con infraestructura institucional y normas culturales favorables.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que las políticas que introducen la educación emprendedora en la infancia pueden fortalecer la generación de iniciativas sociopreneuriales, mientras que la formación posterior requiere entornos institucionales propicios para ser eficaz.
stories.paperTitle: When education sticks: early imprints and sociopreneurship in emerging economies
stories.originalAbstract: This study examines how entrepreneurship education and training (EET) influences sociopreneurship in emerging economies. Drawing on dynamic imprinting theory, we argue that EET received at different stages of life leaves imprints of unequal durability, and that the expression of those imprints depends on supportive institutional conditions. Using Global Entrepreneurship Monitor Adult Population Survey and National Expert Survey data from 26 emerging economies from 2002 to 2022, we distinguish between basic-school and post-school EET and assess how commercial and professional infrastructure, country-level cultural and social norms shape their relationship with sociopreneurship. The findings show that basic-school EET is positively associated with sociopreneurship, suggesting that earlier educational exposure creates more durable prosocial and opportunity-oriented imprints. By contrast, post-school EET is weak or insignificant on average but becomes positively associated with sociopreneurship where institutional infrastructure and cultural norms are more supportive. These results extend dynamic imprinting theory by showing that educational imprints vary by timing and that institutions operate not merely as background conditions but as mechanisms that reactivate latent imprints. The study contributes to research on entrepreneurship education and social entrepreneurship and offers policy implications for early educational intervention and ecosystem development in emerging economies.

stories.headline: Ansiedad regulada potencia juicio financiero bajo incertidumbre
stories.finding: El artículo plantea que la ansiedad, cuando es proporcional, funciona como señal reguladora que aumenta la vigilancia, la detección temprana de pérdidas, la evaluación cautelosa del riesgo, la postergación de la acción y la monitorización disciplinada de carteras. En contraste, la ansiedad sobreactivada produce fijación de amenaza, estrechamiento cognitivo y ventas de pánico.
stories.takeaway: Comprender la naturaleza dialéctica de la ansiedad permite a clínicos y profesionales financieros diseñar estrategias que modulen el arousal, favoreciendo decisiones más equilibradas y evitando conductas financieras desadaptativas.
stories.paperTitle: Rethinking Anxiety in Neurofinance: A Dialectical Framework
stories.originalAbstract: The article reconsiders anxiety in neurofinance by treating it not only as a source of bias or pathology but also as a regulatory signal that may support financial judgment under uncertainty. Drawing on psychoanalytic theory, affective neuroscience, cognitive psychology, and behavioral finance, the study develops a selective and structured narrative review of the literature on anxiety, threat anticipation, loss processing, ambiguity, reward–punishment learning, attention, and impulse control. Its starting point is Freud’s concept of anxiety as a danger signal, which is extended through contemporary evidence on amygdala–prefrontal regulation, autonomic arousal, vigilance, and decision-making under risk and ambiguity. The central argument is that anxiety has a dialectical structure. When proportionate and regulated, it may enhance vigilance, early loss detection, cautious risk evaluation, delayed action, and disciplined portfolio monitoring. When overactivated, the same signal may produce threat fixation, cognitive narrowing, asymmetrical learning from losses, excessive liquidity preference, panic selling, and reactive decision-making. The article therefore proposes a tension-based framework in which anxiety operates between adaptive regulation and maladaptive dysregulation. This framework connects individual affective calibration to broader financial behavior without reducing anxiety to either a clinical disorder or a simple cognitive bias. The article contributes to neurofinance by showing how anxiety may function as both a stabilizing and destabilizing force in financial decision-making.

stories.hook: ¿Cuántos sobrevivientes de terremoto desarrollan duelo prolongado?
stories.headline: Casi un cuarto de sobrevivientes del terremoto turco con enfermedad crónica presentan duelo prolongado
stories.finding: En una muestra de 143 adultos con enfermedad crónica tras el terremoto de 2023 en Turquía, el 23,8 % cumplió criterios de duelo prolongado (PG‑13). La muerte traumática de un familiar de primer grado y ser jubilado aumentaron la prevalencia, alcanzando el 50 % en jubilados (p < 0.001).
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo alerta sobre la alta vulnerabilidad al duelo prolongado en poblaciones con enfermedad crónica tras desastres, indicando la necesidad de intervenciones tempranas y seguimiento específico, especialmente en jubilados que presentan mayor riesgo.
stories.paperTitle: Exploring the bereavement experiences and prevalence of prolonged grief disorder among 2023 Turkish earthquake survivors with advanced chronic disease: a mixed methods study
stories.originalAbstract: OBJECTIVE: While traumatic experience of a loved one's death and having a chronic disease are both risk factors for prolonged grief disorder, there are no published studies on bereavement among earthquake survivors with advanced chronic disease. The objective of this study is to explore the bereavement experiences and prevalence of prolonged grief disorder (PGD) among 2023 Türkiye earthquake survivors with advanced chronic diseases. DESIGN/SETTING: A mixed methods design of cross-sectional survey using the Prolonged Grief Scale (PG-13) and semi-structured interviews was used to provide a detailed understanding of the grief phenomenon in the context of bereaved adults with advanced chronic disease after the earthquake in Türkiye. PARTICIPANTS: 143 participants completed the survey, and interviews were conducted with 12 bereaved survivors with advanced chronic disease. RESULTS: Our results indicated a prevalence of PGD among bereaved adults of 23.8%. The traumatic death of first-degree relatives was associated with a higher PGD prevalence (p<0.001). PGD developed in 50% of retirees (n=6). Six themes were identified: (1) bereavement reactions, (2) coping style, (3) disrupted grieving, (4) impact of grief on chronic disease, (5) moving forward and (6) unmet needs. CONCLUSIONS: We recommend a person-centred bereavement care that prioritises early identification and reduction of prolonged grief risk factors. We propose a framework for bereaved survivors to use in the development of an effective bereavement service model. This model may be used by mental health professionals and policymakers to respond sensitively to the values, needs and preferences of bereaved survivors who have experienced the unnatural death of a loved one.

stories.hook: ¿Qué intervenciones mejoran la atención en niños con TDAH?
stories.headline: Revisión sistemática revela evidencia fragmentada de estrategias cognitivas en TDAH
stories.finding: La revisión incluyó trece ensayos controlados aleatorizados con 1.308 participantes que evaluaron intervenciones no farmacológicas para el rendimiento cognitivo en niños y adolescentes con TDAH. Los resultados, sintetizados narrativamente, mostraron una gran heterogeneidad y ausencia de conclusiones firmes sobre su eficacia.
stories.takeaway: Este panorama subraya la necesidad de ensayos más rigurosos y estandarizados para guiar la práctica clínica y optimizar intervenciones cognitivo-conductuales en el TDAH.
stories.paperTitle: Therapeutic Strategies for Cognitive Performance in Children With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
stories.originalAbstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is among the most common neurodevelopmental disorders of childhood and is characterized by impaired attention, inhibitory control, working memory, and related executive functions. Medication mainly targets core symptoms, and a growing number of non-pharmacological and adjunctive strategies have been tested for their effects on cognitive performance. Randomized evidence is fragmented across intervention types. This review aimed to systematically review randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between January 2015 and 2026 that evaluated therapeutic strategies for cognitive performance in children and adolescents with ADHD. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), and PsycINFO for RCTs published between January 2015 and September 2026. The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidance. Risk of bias was appraised with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool, and findings were synthesised narratively. Thirteen RCTs involving 1,308 participants met the criteria: computerized cognitive training (five trials), physical activity or exergaming (two), eicosapentaenoic acid supplementation (one), digital therapeutics (two), neurofeedback or transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) (two), and virtual reality training (one). Computerized training improved mainly trained or closely related domains such as visuospatial working memory and sustained attention, with inconsistent far transfer. Exergaming improved reaction times in inhibition and switching after both single-session and eight-week exposure. Eicosapentaenoic acid improved focused attention, most clearly in children with low baseline levels. A video-game-based digital therapeutic improved objectively measured attention in 348 children. Neurofeedback (n = 144) and multi-session tDCS (n = 50) showed no specific cognitive benefit over sham. Five trials had low risk of bias, seven had some concerns, and one had high risk. Several non-pharmacological strategies can improve selected domains of cognitive performance in children with ADHD, but benefits are domain-specific, usually short-term, and weaker in sham-controlled, blinded designs. No single strategy is superior across domains. Choice of therapy should be individualized, and larger, blinded, longer-term trials with standardized cognitive endpoints are needed.

stories.hook: ¿Qué estilo parental impulsa el rendimiento escolar?
stories.headline: El estilo parental autoritativo se vincula fuertemente al rendimiento académico
stories.finding: En una muestra de 509 alumnos de primaria pública en Lagos, el estilo parental autoritativo mostró una correlación positiva con el desempeño en Matemáticas y Lengua (r = .45, p < .05). Este hallazgo sugiere que prácticas parentales que combinan exigencia y apoyo están asociadas a mejores resultados académicos.
stories.takeaway: Este dato orienta a profesionales y padres a fomentar un estilo autoritativo, combinando estructura y calidez, para potenciar el aprendizaje y reducir la brecha de rendimiento en contextos de alta vulnerabilidad.
stories.paperTitle: Techno-Regulated Parenting Frameworks and Foundational Learning Poverty: An Ex-Post Facto Analysis of Pupils’ Intellectual Engagement in Lagos State Public Schools
stories.journal: International Journal for Early Childhood and Educational Research
stories.originalAbstract: This study investigated the relationship and predictive influence of perceived parenting styles on the academic performance of pupils in public primary schools in Lagos State, Nigeria, where a visible decline in elementary-level literacy and numeracy has become a pressing concern. Grounded in Bandura’s Social Learning Theory and Bowlby’s Attachment Theory, the study adopted ex-post facto research design. 4 hypotheses were tested at .05 alpha level of significance. Through a multi-stage sampling procedure, a sample of 509 upper primary school pupils (Primary 5 and 6) was selected from public schools within the state. Data collection for the study was done using the Perceived Parenting Styles Scale (PPSS) while official terminal examination records in Mathematics and English Language/Literacy were used to measure their academic performance. Inferential statistics (Pearson Product-Moment Correlation and Multiple Regression Analysis) were utilized to test the hypotheses. The empirical findings revealed that the authoritative parenting style has a strong, statistically significant positive correlation with academic performance (r = .45, p < .05), indicating that households combining high emotional responsiveness with balanced behavioral control directly foster superior classroom achievement. Conversely, the authoritarian parenting style exhibited a significant negative correlation with academic output (r = -.09, p < .05) and was singled out by the regression coefficients as a heavy, powerful negative predictor of achievement, proving that rigid, low-warmth environments driven by harsh punitive measures severely impair cognitive focus. Permissive and neglectful parenting styles demonstrated weak positive correlations (r = .13 and r = .09 respectively, p < .05). The study concluded that perceived parenting styles are undeniable predictors of pupil’s academic performance, and that particularly rigid authoritarianism undermines foundational academic capabilities. It was recommended that Lagos State Government and school administrators should collaborate to deploy targeted sensitization modules via Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs), while school guidance counselors design localised community outreach interventions that help parents balance household realities with active academic support at home.

It was recommended that Lagos State Government and school administrators should collaborate to deploy targeted sensitization modules via Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs), while school guidance counselors design localised community outreach interventions that help parents balance household realities with active academic support at home.

stories.hook: ¿Puede el BDNF ser la clave del dolor crónico?
stories.headline: Niveles elevados de BDNF vinculados a la sensibilización central en dolor crónico
stories.finding: El BDNF actúa como neurotransmisor y neuromodulador que regula la plasticidad sináptica y potencia la sensibilización central. Estudios revisados indican que los niveles de BDNF están consistentemente elevados en diversos trastornos de dolor crónico.
stories.takeaway: Identificar al BDNF como biomarcador objetivo abre posibilidades para diagnósticos tempranos y terapias que modulen su señalización, ofreciendo nuevas estrategias para interrumpir la centralización del dolor y mejorar el manejo clínico.
stories.paperTitle: The Role of the Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor in Chronic Pain: Links to Central Sensitization and Neuroinflammation
stories.originalAbstract: Chronic pain is sustained, in part, through the intricate process of central sensitization (CS), marked by maladaptive neuroplasticity and neuronal hyperexcitability within central pain pathways. Accumulating evidence suggests that CS is also driven by neuroinflammation in the peripheral and central nervous system. In any chronic disease, the search for perpetuating factors is crucial in identifying therapeutic targets and developing primary preventive strategies. The brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) emerges as a critical regulator of synaptic plasticity, serving as both a neurotransmitter and neuromodulator. Mounting evidence supports BDNF’s pro-nociceptive role, spanning from its pain-sensitizing capacity across multiple levels of nociceptive pathways to its intricate involvement in CS and neuroinflammation. Moreover, consistently elevated BDNF levels are observed in various chronic pain disorders. To comprehensively understand the profound impact of BDNF in chronic pain, we delve into its key characteristics, focusing on its role in underlying molecular mechanisms contributing to chronic pain. Additionally, we also explore the potential utility of BDNF as an objective biomarker for chronic pain. This discussion encompasses emerging therapeutic approaches aimed at modulating BDNF expression, offering insights into addressing the intricate complexities of chronic pain.
